alternates.summary: Merryn Somerset Webb talks with Alex Edmans, author of "The Madness of Markets: Why Smart Investors Make Crazy Decisions – And How to Exploit Them," about why even sophisticated investors struggle to overcome the psychological biases that shape their decisions. Markets are driven by humans, and humans are emotional. Edmans explains how understanding the influence of emotion, herd behavior and over-confidence can help investors make better decisions — and potentially achieve better returns. (Source: Bloomberg)
alternates.title: How to Outsmart Your Investing Instincts

articles.summary: Speaking at a tech forum in Kyoto, Masayoshi Son called for global cooperation on AI safeguards, warning that superintelligence could pose a greater threat than conflict between humans if misused. Bloomberg tech editor Mayumi Negishi said the caution marks a notable shift in tone from the longtime technology optimist, though Son remains strongly bullish on AI. He estimates AI machines could account for at least 20% of global GDP—about $46 trillion—by 2040, and suggested investors could see 50-fold returns over roughly 15 years. Negishi also noted that SoftBank has committed about $65 billion to OpenAI. Son continues to describe AI as a potential source of hope and greater happiness, while emphasizing that its capabilities and associated risks are growing rapidly. Original filename: 20261005_015541_Masayoshi_Son_Warns_AI_Could_Become_Super_Dangerous_in_the.mp4 (Source: Bloomberg)
articles.title: SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son Has Rare Cautionary Note on AI Safety
